writeup: TIC 41996755 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 9.5631 days. The TESS mission detected a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 10.89 percent, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 290.0 in the automated search. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 69.5, though the centroid offset of 1.7 arcsec warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel object. The machine-learning screening score of 0.70 indicates the pipeline's model considers this a likely real target, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
